record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: What theoretical framework, experiment set, or combination of both could resolve the open elementary-particle questions collected in this section, including whether there is a Dirac ether fluid, whether Dirac's 1951 electron theory can remove the infinity problem and reconcile quantum-mechanical and electrodynamical descriptions of the electron, what dynamical mechanism underlies the Koide lepton-mass relation, whether neutrinos have mass, whether preon or rishon models outperform conventional quantum chromodynamics, whether quark confinement has a physical explanation, whether quantum chromodynamics is linked to quantum fluid dynamics, whether isolated quarks or rishons can exist or be produced, whether quark, rishon, and neutrino properties admit quaternionic, multivalued-logic, or Gross-Pitaevskii-type explanations, how gravity affects quark charges, whether quark charges or masses can be altered or converted into energy, and whether anti-hydrogen signatures, ring models of the electron, or hidden neutrinos in ordinary matter can be detected or explained consistently?

evidence.quote: (i) Is there a Dirac æther fluid? [2]  (ii) Can Dirac’s recent theory 1951 solve the infinity problem?
Now from these ‘known’ questions, we can also ask some new questions for further development of theoretical physics:

(xx) Could we find a theoretical basis for Quantum Mechanics and Quantum Electrodynamics which automatically includes anti-hydrogen in the theory?  (xxi) Could we find neutrinos inside the human body?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Propose a theoretical framework, an experimental program, or a combination of both capable of resolving the following cluster of open questions in elementary-particle physics and quantum theory:

1. Does a "Dirac ether" — a relativistically invariant fluid-like vacuum medium of the type proposed by Dirac — exist as a physical entity?
2. Can Dirac's 1951 reformulation of electron theory (a nonlinear, ether-based extension of the Dirac equation) eliminate the ultraviolet/self-energy infinities of the electron and produce a single consistent description that unifies the quantum-mechanical and the classical-electrodynamical pictures of the electron?
3. What dynamical mechanism, if any, underlies the empirical Koide relation for the charged-lepton masses,
   (m_e + m_μ + m_τ) / (√m_e + √m_μ + √m_τ)² = 2/3 ?
4. Do neutrinos have nonzero rest mass, and if so what are the absolute masses and the mass hierarchy?
5. Do composite-substructure models of quarks and leptons (preon or rishon models) yield predictions that surpass those of conventional quantum chromodynamics (QCD)?
6. Is there a derivation from first principles of the physical mechanism responsible for quark confinement in QCD?
7. Is there a precise mathematical correspondence between QCD and a "quantum fluid dynamics" describing the QCD vacuum or hadronic interior as a quantum fluid?
8. Can isolated free quarks or rishons exist as asymptotic states, and can they be produced and detected?
9. Do the properties of quarks, rishons, and neutrinos admit consistent reformulations in terms of (a) quaternionic quantum mechanics, (b) multivalued logics, or (c) Gross–Pitaevskii–type nonlinear Schrödinger condensate descriptions?
10. How does the gravitational interaction affect the effective electric charge of quarks?
11. Under what (if any) physical processes can the electric charge or rest mass of a quark be altered, or be converted directly into energy?
12. Is there a consistent quantum field theory in which anti-hydrogen arises automatically, and are there detectable signatures of cosmic anti-hydrogen?
13. Can a "ring" (extended, toroidal) model of the electron be made compatible with relativistic quantum theory?
14. Could a population of "hidden" neutrinos be present within ordinary matter (e.g., the human body) and be experimentally detected?

The problem is to give, for as many of items (1)–(14) as possible, either a definitive theoretical resolution, a feasible experimental test, or a rigorous demonstration of inconsistency.
artifact.status_search_result: These are long-standing speculative and foundational questions in particle physics. Several sub-questions remain unsolved as of 2026: the dynamical origin of the Koide relation has no accepted derivation; absolute neutrino masses and hierarchy remain unknown (KATRIN, JUNO, cosmology still bounding); quark confinement lacks a rigorous first-principles proof (related to the Clay Yang–Mills mass-gap problem); preon/rishon models remain speculative without experimental confirmation; the Dirac ether and ring-electron models are not part of the Standard Model and have no accepted status. No comprehensive resolution of the full list exists.

status_evidence.title: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap (Clay Mathematics Institute)
status_evidence.snippet: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang–Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap.
status_evidence.claim: The mathematical problem closely related to quark confinement remains an open Millennium Prize Problem.

status_evidence.title: Koide formula - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: There is currently no accepted explanation for why the Koide formula holds.
status_evidence.claim: No accepted dynamical mechanism for the Koide lepton-mass relation is known.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino mass - Particle Data Group review
status_evidence.snippet: Absolute neutrino masses and the mass ordering remain undetermined experimentally.
status_evidence.claim: Whether and what masses neutrinos have in absolute terms is still being measured.
